source.title: Insights on representational similarity in neural networks with canonical correlation
source.authors: Ari S. Morcos; M. Raghu; Samy Bengio

record.tranche_reason: Measures representation similarity with projection-weighted CCA and compares it across network widths, training conditions, and independently initialized networks; this is a conceptual test rather than a reproduction of the original convergence method.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures pairwise representation similarity across independently initialized CIFAR-10 networks, including a width sweep. It also compares similarity measures and reports train-versus-test differences. RNN training-time and sequence-time analyses, and the synthetic signal/noise demonstration, do not test these claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures projection-weighted CCA distance between same-topology CIFAR-10 ConvNets from different random initializations. It does so under true versus random labels, across a width sweep, and across 200 networks with different learning rates. These are direct measurements of cross-seed convergence (V3) and of a within-family size and accuracy trend (V1). It also compares similarity measures (V6) and reports incomplete, hyperparameter-clustered convergence (V7). The method differs from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that layer representations contain stable 'signal' and unstable 'noise' parts, which motivates projection weighting. They further conclude that RNNs converge bottom-up over training and that RNN hidden states vary nonlinearly across sequence steps. They suggest that cross-seed CCA distance may predict test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses projection-weighted canonical correlation analysis, developed from SVCCA, rather than the methods of the cited original convergence studies; compares layer representations across networks, widths, and training conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on similarity metric: cosine and Euclidean distance fail to reveal some reported differences; unweighted CCA and SVCCA miss layer-specific details. Results also differ between training and test data for memorizing networks, and between early layers, later layers, and softmax.
record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2018)
record.problems: The principal network comparisons use groups of five networks; many reported distances are available only in figures. The CIFAR-10 width experiment holds the architecture family and dataset fixed, so it does not establish broad cross-architecture, cross-objective, cross-data, or cross-modal convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results omitted. RNN training-time and sequence-time analyses and synthetic signal/noise experiments were excluded because they do not measure convergence across independently trained models in the versions at issue.

untested.parts: Different architectures, objectives, datasets or modalities. Scaling beyond small CIFAR-10 ConvNets. Only width within one architecture family is varied.
Entire version: no vision-language or paired-caption comparison.
Identification of specific shared features or units. Settings beyond CIFAR-10 ConvNets.
Entire version: no mapping, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired transfer is tested. CCA's linear invariance is assumed, not evaluated as a low-loss map.
Entire version: no interpretable features or circuits are compared.
Neighbour-count or kernel settings. Out-of-distribution inputs, beyond the train-versus-test softmax contrast.
Whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain alignment. Plateau with scale is not tested in trained networks.

missing.what: Cosine and Euclidean distance fail to show that larger networks converge to more similar solutions, whereas PWCCA shows it. This is metric dependence of the width/convergence trend.
Trained-network PWCCA distance across the width sweep falls from about 0.47 to 0.28. These are the actual magnitudes behind r9, currently only mentioned in r11's note.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source. V1's link rests on a within-family width sweep of identically designed CNNs. It shows scale and capability tracking cross-seed convergence, not convergence across architectures or objectives, so the V1 support is narrow. The r11 initialization control strengthens V1 rather than limiting it. The V7 links on early-layer and softmax rows were removed because those rows do not bear on incompleteness or its causes. The RNN and toy results were correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: The width sweep tests similarity across sizes for CNNs of the same architecture family trained on CIFAR-10. It does not test different architectures, objectives, datasets, or modalities generally, nor whether capability rises across those settings.
No paired image-caption or vision-language comparison.
Tests same-topology CNNs with different initializations on CIFAR-10, including true-label and random-label conditions. It does not identify or interpret shared individual features or units.

CCA is invariant to linear transformations, but the study does not test whether a mapping between model representations transfers with little loss, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits.

Tests dependence on similarity measure and, for some comparisons, training versus test inputs. It does not systematically vary CCA settings such as neighbour count or evaluate general out-of-distribution inputs.

Compares generalizing and memorizing models, reports nonzero distances among generalizing networks, and finds learning-rate-associated clusters. It does not establish whether shared data or objectives explain alignment versus a common model of reality.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on unmodified labels (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance within groups of independently initialized networks.
rows.note: The text says early-layer networks were equally similar regardless of whether they generalized or memorized.
rows.check: Early layers are equally similar for generalizing and memorizing groups, which is cross-seed convergence. This does not test V7's causal claim, so the V7 link is dropped.

rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance within groups of independently initialized networks.

conditions.value: same fixed random permutation for all networks; memorizing

rows.note: The text says early-layer networks were equally similar regardless of whether they generalized or memorized.
rows.check: Same as r1. The V7 link is dropped.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on unmodified labels (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance within groups of independently initialized networks.
rows.value: figure only; distances remain well above zero
rows.note: Generalizing networks are more similar in later layers than memorizing networks, but the text says their distances remain well above zero and their solutions remain diverse.
rows.check: For V3 the state is partial: later-layer generalizing networks are more similar than memorizers, but the text says distances stay 'well above zero'. For V7 this is the incompleteness the version predicts, so it counts as observed.

source_check.correct: V3: partial. V7: observed for the incomplete-alignment component; causal explanations are untested.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, paragraph describing later-layer distances; Figure 3.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state does not fit both linked versions: incomplete convergence is itself the effect predicted by V7.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on randomized labels (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance within groups of independently initialized networks.

conditions.value: same fixed random permutation for all networks; memorizing

rows.note: The paper reports less similarity than for generalizing networks in later layers.
rows.check: Memorizing networks are substantially less similar in later layers. This bears on V3 under a memorization condition, not on V7's causal claim.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on true labels versus randomized labels (aggregate groups of 5)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance between generalizing and memorizing networks.
rows.baseline: within-group distances shown for the generalizing and memorizing groups
rows.value: figure only; memorizing networks are reported as similarly diverse among themselves as across the generalizing group
rows.note: The text describes memorizing networks as about as similar to one another as to a generalizing network.
rows.check: This is a between-group comparison of networks trained on different labellings. It does not measure convergence among identically trained models. It is a comparator, not a convergence result for any version.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on true or randomized labels (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance at the softmax layer.
rows.value: figure only; both groups reported as highly similar
rows.note: The paper attributes the high similarity to all networks reaching near-zero training loss.
rows.check: Softmax similarity on training data is near-identical. The authors attribute this to near-zero training loss, so it is largely forced by fitting the same labels. The V7 link is dropped.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on true labels (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance at the softmax layer.
rows.value: figure only; similar but not identical solutions
rows.note: The text says generalizing networks converge to similar, though not identical, softmax solutions on test data.
rows.check: 'Similar (though not identical)' test-set softmax solutions match V3's wording, so the state is observed rather than partial. The V7 link is dropped.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on randomized labels (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance at the softmax layer.

conditions.value: same fixed random permutation for all networks; memorizing

rows.value: figure only; memorizing networks did not converge to similar solutions
rows.note: The text says memorizing networks use diverse strategies on test data.
rows.check: Memorizing networks do not converge at the test-set softmax. The V7 link is dropped.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets at each width (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise projection-weighted CCA distances among networks trained from different random initializations at each width.

conditions.value: same convolutional architecture, layers scaled equally

rows.baseline: narrower networks in the width sweep
rows.value: figure only; larger networks converged to much more similar solutions
rows.note: The comparison used a random subset of 128 final-layer filters to control for representation-size differences.
rows.check: For V1, this is a single architecture family scaled in width on one dataset, so it falls short of V1's cross-architecture scope. Distances were computed on a random subset of 128 final-layer filters.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 ConvNets across width sweep (pairs of networks; aggregate relationship)
rows.operation_detail: Related pairwise CCA distance to test accuracy across network pairs.

conditions.value: correlation between test accuracy and pairwise CCA distance

rows.measure: Correlation between test accuracy and pairwise CCA distance
rows.note: Higher test accuracy was associated with lower pairwise CCA distance.
rows.check: The value -0.96 is stated in the text. Note that CCA distance is computed on training data while accuracy is test accuracy.

rows.subject: Groups of 5 CIFAR-10 ConvNets at initialization (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured CCA distance across widths at initialization and after training.
rows.value: approximately 0.67 to 0.63; plateaued past approximately 1000 filters
rows.note: The paper contrasts this moderate decrease with the larger decrease after training, from approximately 0.47 to 0.28.
rows.check: This is a control. At initialization the distance falls only from about 0.67 to 0.63, against about 0.47 to 0.28 after training. That shows the width trend comes from training rather than from a size artefact, which supports V1 rather than limiting it. It does not bear on V6; the trend is observed as a training effect.

source_check.correct: State=partial for the weak width trend at initialization: distance decreases approximately 0.67 to 0.63 and plateaus beyond approximately 1000 filters, versus approximately 0.47 to 0.28 after training. Increasing capability is untested in this initialization control.
source_check.problem: Observed overstates the small initialization effect relative to the trained-network trend.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on true or randomized labels (aggregate groups of 5)
rows.operation_detail: Compared cosine and Euclidean distances with CCA for generalizing, memorizing, and between-group comparisons.
rows.value: figure only; these metrics did not reveal the later-layer difference between generalizing and memorizing groups
rows.note: The paper explicitly contrasts these metrics with CCA's ability to reveal the difference.
rows.check: The state is relative to V6, whose effect is dependence on the measure. Cosine and Euclidean distance fail to show the later-layer difference that PWCCA shows, so metric dependence is observed, not absent.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on true or randomized labels (aggregate groups of 5)
rows.operation_detail: Compared unweighted CCA and SVCCA with projection-weighted CCA.
rows.value: figure only; same broad pattern, but misses the increased similarity of generalizing networks in the final two layers and overestimates early-layer distances
rows.note: The text reports the metric-specific differences.
rows.check: Unweighted CCA gives the same broad pattern but misses the final-two-layer increase and overestimates early-layer distances. This is moderate metric dependence.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained on true or randomized labels (aggregate groups of 5)
rows.operation_detail: Compared unweighted SVCCA with projection-weighted CCA.
rows.value: figure only; same broad pattern, but misses the increased similarity of generalizing networks in the final two layers and overestimates early-layer distances
rows.note: The text reports the metric-specific differences.
rows.check: SVCCA overestimates early-layer distances. The text attributes the missed final-layer feature to unweighted CCA specifically.

rows.subject: 200 CIFAR-10 ConvNets with identical topology (aggregate pairwise comparisons)
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise projection-weighted CCA distance at the eighth layer and examined the distance matrix.
rows.value: figure only; five distinct clusters, one highly dissimilar to the other four
rows.note: The clusters align with learning-rate groups; networks had similar training loss and many had similar test accuracy.
rows.check: The 200 networks form five learning-rate-aligned clusters, one highly dissimilar to the rest. For V3 this is partial convergence. For V7 it is observed incompleteness that depends on optimization hyperparameters. Network sizes are not stated; presumably the default architecture.

source_check.correct: V3: partial. V7: observed for incomplete convergence and optimization-dependent clustering; shared-data/objective causal explanations are untested.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state does not distinguish partial V3 convergence from observed V7 incompleteness.

relationships.condition: Same-architecture CIFAR-10 ConvNets trained at width multipliers from 0.25 to 7.0
relationships.reason: Wider networks converge to more similar solutions (r9). Distance correlates with test accuracy at -0.96 (r10). The trend is largely absent at initialization (r11).
relationships.display_finding: Wider networks converged to more similar solutions, with representational distance correlating with test accuracy at −0.96 and little corresponding trend at initialization.

relationships.condition: Early layers, softmax on training data, test-set softmax of generalizing networks, and wider networks
relationships.reason: Networks from different seeds converge to similar solutions in early layers (r1, r2). Generalizing test-set softmax solutions are similar but not identical (r7). Training-data softmax is near-identical (r6). Convergence grows with width (r9).
relationships.display_finding: Early-layer representations were similar across seeds and convergence increased with width, while softmax representations were nearly identical on training data and similar but distinct on test data for generalizing networks.

source_check.condition: Early layers, softmax on training data, test-set softmax of generalizing networks, and wider networks
source_check.reason: Figures 3, 4 and A10 report shared representations across seeds under these conditions. Training-softmax agreement follows near-zero training loss on the same labels.

relationships.condition: Later layers, networks trained on random labels, and networks trained with different learning rates
relationships.reason: Later-layer distances stay well above zero (r3) and are larger for memorizers (r4). Memorizers diverge at the test-set softmax (r8). Networks split into learning-rate clusters (r15).
relationships.display_finding: Later-layer distances remained above zero and increased with memorization, including divergence at the test-set softmax; representations also clustered by learning rate.

relationships.display_finding: Cosine and Euclidean distance missed the difference between generalizing and memorizing networks, while unweighted CCA and SVCCA missed features and overestimated early-layer distances.
